body:
## User scenario

An embedded browser coding environment uses the no-COI SDK to let an agent read, list, edit and remove project files. Ordinary project operations should have a structured worker-owned interface, without the embedding app constructing JavaScript strings or using files as an RPC return channel.

## Gap in published 0.7.0

- `Sandbox.fs` / `RuntimeFs` expose only `readFile` and `writeFile`.
- Listing and other filesystem operations require guest `node:fs` calls through `runtime.eval()`.
- The runtime worker prints the evaluated value and returns `value: undefined`, although `EvalResult` declares a value field. A host wanting structured results can end up writing JSON into a temporary file, reading it through FS RPC, then evaluating another command to remove it.
- Workbench already has a richer `ProjectFiles` interface: `readdir`, `mkdir`, `rename`, `remove`, mutation outcomes and notifications. This is a no-COI SDK interface gap, not an absence of filesystem support in rifty.

## Requested outcome

Expose ordinary project filesystem operations through the no-COI SDK, reusing existing filesystem ownership and error/persistence handling. At minimum cover directory listing, stat, mkdir, rename and removal alongside read/write.

Also make programmatic evaluation's result contract explicit: either provide a supported structured-result operation or clearly distinguish console-oriented eval from it. Returning structured data should not require persistent temporary files. Exact method names and serialization limits are design choices, not proposed commitments to an arbitrary RPC framework.

## Acceptance

- A packed SDK consumer lists, creates, renames and removes real project files using public methods, with paths consistent with existing `RuntimeFs`.
- Mutation completion and errors retain honest persistence semantics, including worker termination and failed OPFS writes.
- If structured evaluation is exposed, unsupported/non-cloneable values and result limits fail explicitly; stdout stays separate from the returned value.
- No temporary project/control files are needed merely to retrieve a directory listing or command result.

Host responsibilities remain tool schemas, allowed paths, UI and model-facing output formatting. Evidence is a static audit of published 0.7.0; this issue does not claim a new runtime reproduction or fix.
title: No-COI SDK: structured project filesystem operations without eval/file RPC
